---
title: "Tool Calling"
description: "A model-assisted workflow in which an application lets a model request approved operations through tools."
term: "Tool Calling"
letter: "T"
category: "AI Agents"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Tool calling lets an AI application connect a model to operations such as
searching documents or checking a database. The model can ask for a tool to
be used, while the application decides whether the request is valid and
allowed.

## Technical explanation

An application describes available tools and their input schemas to a
model. The model may return a structured request; the application validates
the request, enforces permissions, executes the implementation, and may
return the result for further model processing. Provider APIs and agent
frameworks use different tool-calling formats.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Tools extend a model's ability to interact with current data and software
systems. They also create security and reliability concerns because
operations may access sensitive information or cause side effects.

## How it works

The host provides tool descriptions and user context. If the model requests
a tool, the host checks the name, arguments, authorization, and applicable
approval requirements before execution. Results are returned to the model
or user, with errors handled explicitly.

The model requests an operation; the host retains control of execution.

## Practical example

A research assistant can request a search tool with a query. The host can
restrict the search to permitted sources, validate the query, execute a
read-only search, and return selected results for the model to summarize.

## Common misconceptions

- Tool calling does not mean the model executes arbitrary code or accesses
  tools directly.
- A declared schema does not replace server-side validation, authorization,
  or safeguards for side effects.
